title: Brazil’s LGPD and the duty to protect personal data

videos.script: Every lesson so far protected the shop's information because losing it would hurt the shop. This one adds a second reason. Some of that information is about people, and the law says the shop owes them something. {{people}} Brazil's general data protection law, the LGPD, has been in force since 2020. It applies to a nine-person bookshop as much as to a bank. {{law}} You will learn what counts as personal data, and the ten legal grounds on which a business may process it. Then the principles the law sets, and the rights each customer can exercise. {{grounds}} Then the part that ties back to this course. A duty to keep the data secure, and a duty to report a serious incident within three working days. {{duty}} Last, who is who: the shop, its suppliers, and the person who answers for the data. {{roles}}
